title: Pricing Control ignores a package's effective_from/effective_to, so a price scheduled for the future is charged today and a retired price is charged forever
reproduction:
node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p5.mjs (route-level, no library shortcuts). It imports app/api/pricing-control/route.ts and app/api/boarding-commercial/route.ts, then:
1. POST /api/boarding-commercial {packageCode:'boarding-24h',petCount:2,scheduledStart:+7d,scheduledEnd:+7d+48h,paymentMode:'prepaid'} -> baseline quote.
2. PATCH /api/pricing-control {entity:'package',id:'canonical_boarding_24h',changes:{active:1,base_price:2500,effective_from:'2027-01-01'},reason:'ops scheduling a price change'} -- effective_from is in the PATCH allow-list at app/api/pricing-control/route.ts (`allowed` for entity 'package' includes 'effective_from','effective_to').
3. Repeat the same customer quote TODAY (system date 2026-08-24).
4. PATCH again to {base_price:150,effective_from:'2026-01-01',effective_to:'2026-01-31'} (a promo that ended 7 months ago) and quote again.
Also reproduced independently for grooming in /tmp/probe/p14.mjs against lib/grooming-governance.ts governGroomingBooking, and for the raw resolver in /tmp/probe/p3.mjs.
expected: resolveLivePrice should only honour a service_packages row whose effective window contains the booking's scheduledStart, i.e. the same predicate every vertical already applies to its own catalogue (`activePackage` in lib/boarding-governance.ts:39, lib/sitting-governance.ts, lib/training-commercial-governance.ts) and the same predicate lib/pricing-engine.ts:11 `activeOn` already applies to dynamic_pricing_rules. A row dated 2027-01-01 must not price a 2026-08-31 stay; a row whose effective_to is 2026-01-31 must fall back to the vertical's catalogue price. Concretely, step 3 should still have returned total 2796 and step 5 should also have returned 2796.
consequence: An operator using the Pricing Control panel exactly as designed - scheduling a price rise for the next quarter, or ending a January promotion by setting effective_to - changes the price customers are charged RIGHT NOW. In the reproduction an identical 2-night, 2-pet Luxury Stay went from Rs 2,796 to Rs 12,500 the instant a 2027-dated row was saved, and to Rs 752 when a long-dead January promo row was saved. The wrong figure is what the customer sees at checkout, what is written to boarding_commercial_quotes.total_amount, what governBoardingBooking then enforces on confirmation, and what lands in booking_payments.amount. The panel shows the operator the effective dates it just stored, so the operator has no way to see that they are not being honoured. This is the single lookup behind Boarding, Pet Sitting, Training and Grooming pricing (lib/live-commercial-quotes.ts, lib/training-commercial-governance.ts:29, lib/grooming-governance.ts:74, lib/live-grooming-governance.ts) and the public /api/live-price-quote the customer grooming flow renders from (app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx:91).
rule_source: lib/pricing-engine.ts:11 `activeOn` (the same module already enforces the effective window for dynamic_pricing_rules); lib/boarding-governance.ts:39 / lib/sitting-governance.ts / lib/training-commercial-governance.ts `activePackage` (every vertical enforces effective_from/effective_to on its own catalogue); app/api/pricing-control/route.ts `allowed` list, which exposes effective_from/effective_to as operator-editable package fields.
suggested_fix: In resolveLivePrice, filter the package row on the booking date the same way rules are filtered: `SELECT * FROM service_packages WHERE package_code=? AND active=1 AND effective_from<=? AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to>=?)` bound with input.scheduledStart.slice(0,10) twice, so a row outside its window falls through to `{price: input.fallbackPrice, source:'fallback_default'}`. app/api/pricing-quote/route.ts:ensureSchema/POST carries the identical unfiltered lookup and needs the same change.

title: A Pet Sitting booking confirmed through /api/canonical-bookings is priced entirely by the client - any amount, any invented package code
reproduction:
node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p8.mjs. Uses a REAL, non-preview actor: host app.pawspace.in (so isDevelopmentPreview is false), app_users row role_code='customer' (permissions ['pricing.view','scheduling.book'] per lib/platform-security.ts:24), customer_identity_links binding that email to CUS-P8, request header oai-authenticated-user-email: cust@example.com. lib/api-gateway.ts:125 maps POST /api/canonical-bookings to exactly 'scheduling.book', which this role holds.
Seed the scheduling graph (scheduling_assignment_decisions status='assigned' + one scheduling_reservations row with service_code='pet_sitting', matching city/zone/customer), then POST /api/canonical-bookings with serviceCode:'pet_sitting' and totalAmount set by the caller. No sittingQuoteId is required or checked on this path (contrast: 'boarding' requires pricing.boardingQuoteId, 'dog_training' requires pricing.trainingQuoteId, 'grooming' runs governGroomingBookingWithLiveMultiPet).
expected: A Pet Sitting confirmation should be governed the way the platform already governs it on its own route: app/api/sitting-bookings/route.ts requires input.sittingQuoteId, calls requireSittingQuoteSandboxCapture, then governSittingBooking, which rejects any submittedTotal that does not equal the server-computed sitting_commercial_quotes.total_amount and any package_code that is not the quote's. An overnight Pet Sitting stay of 12h for one pet is Rs 1598 from the seeded catalogue (lib/sitting-governance.ts packages: sitting-overnight basePrice 799 x 2 billable units); a request claiming Rs 1 or Rs 0, or naming package 'free-plan', should be a 409, not a 201 confirmed booking.
consequence: An ordinary signed-in customer - not staff, holding only pricing.view and scheduling.book - can confirm a real Pet Sitting booking at a price of their own choosing. The reproduction produced a durable canonical_bookings row with status 'confirmed' and total_amount 0, a provider_work_orders row dispatching a real sitter, and a booking_payments row reading amount 0 / status 'captured'. The sitter is scheduled and will show up; provider payout, revenue recognition, GST and every downstream report read total_amount from this row. The package_code is not validated at all, so the booking can also be labelled with a package that does not exist, breaking any reader that joins on it. The governed route exists and is what lib/sitting-booking-client.ts uses - this is a second, ungoverned door onto the same tables.
rule_source: app/api/sitting-bookings/route.ts + lib/sitting-governance.ts governSittingBooking ('Sitting amount does not match the server quote', 409) - the platform's own definition of a correctly priced Pet Sitting confirmation. The in-file comment at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:391 ('Pet Sitting on this path is client-priced (no server quote yet)') acknowledges the gap but the governed path now exists.
suggested_fix: Treat pet_sitting on this route the way boarding and dog_training are already treated: require pricing.sittingQuoteId, call governSittingBooking, and set `governed` from its result rather than from input.totalAmount/input.packageCode. If /api/canonical-bookings is not meant to serve Pet Sitting at all now that /api/sitting-bookings exists, remove 'pet_sitting' from the `services` set at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:26 and return 409 pointing at the governed route.

title: Grooming policy CREATE stores an unvalidated enforcement_mode; anything but exactly "enforce" silently becomes "observe", which forces 100% refund and waives every cancellation/reschedule rule
pattern: H2 (unknown value normalised to the permissive branch) + gate polarity
reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p10.mjs (probe) and /tmp/pj/p9.mjs (unit matrix).
1. installHooks(); fresh in-memory D1.
2. POST /api/grooming-commercial-policy with body {cityId:"city_blr",policyCode:"grooming-blr",enforcementMode:"Enforce",cancellationCutoffMinutes:1440,refundPercentBeforeCutoff:100,refundPercentAfterCutoff:0,rescheduleCutoffMinutes:1440,rescheduleAllowedAfterCutoff:false,maxReschedules:1,rescheduleFeeType:"flat",rescheduleFeeValue:500,multiPetMax:1,effectiveFrom:"2026-01-01",reason:"City launch policy"}
3. Read the stored row, then resolveGroomingPolicy(db,"city_blr","zone_1").
4. Seed a grooming booking BK_P1 (total 2000, status assigned, payment captured 2000) whose scheduled_start is now+60min - i.e. INSIDE the 1440-minute cutoff, so the policy prices the refund at 0%.
5. POST /api/grooming-booking-change {bookingId:"BK_P1",customerId:"cust_P",action:"cancel",reason:"late cancel"}.
6. PATCH the same policy with changes:{enforcement_mode:"Enforce"} for contrast.
expected: Either (a) POST validates enforcement_mode against ['observe','enforce'] exactly as PATCH already does at app/api/grooming-commercial-policy/route.ts:11, returning 400 for "Enforce"; or (b) rowToPolicy/parsePolicySnapshot fail closed on an unrecognised value (treat unknown as 'enforce', or throw a configuration error) rather than defaulting to the permissive 'observe'. A refund of 0% was configured; a refund case of 0 (or a 409) is the expected outcome, not a 2000 refund case.
consequence: Real money. A pricing manager launches a city with an enforcing cancellation policy - 24h cutoff, 0% late refund, one free reschedule, 500 reschedule fee, one pet max - and every one of those rules is silently inert because a single mis-cased string was accepted by the create endpoint that the update endpoint rejects. Every late customer cancellation raises a 100%-of-captured-amount refund case (2000 of 2000 measured), every reschedule is free and unlimited, and the multi-pet cap at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:195 (guarded on enforcementMode==="enforce") never fires. Finance reconciles refunds it should never have owed; the operator reading the policy row sees "Enforce" while every API response says "observe", so the two surfaces disagree and nothing alerts.
rule_source: The repository's own contract: PATCH on the same table already enforces ['observe','enforce'] (app/api/grooming-commercial-policy/route.ts:11), and lib/grooming-policy-governance.ts:42 evaluateBookingChange treats every non-"observe" value as enforcing. Only the CREATE path and the row parser disagree.
suggested_fix: Add the same allow-list validation to POST (reject anything not in ['observe','enforce'], along with the numeric range checks PATCH performs), and change rowToPolicy/parsePolicySnapshot so an unrecognised enforcement_mode fails closed - either throw a configuration-required error like resolveGroomingPolicy already does for a missing policy, or map unknown to 'enforce'.

title: A rejected set_mandate call destroys the category's verification mandate: the DELETE commits, the re-INSERT does not, and defaults are never re-seeded
expected: Either the whole mandate replacement commits or none of it does. A 500 answer must leave the previous mandate exactly as it was. Duplicated / empty entries in verificationTypes should be de-duplicated (or refused) BEFORE the DELETE, the way unknown type codes already are at line 96.
consequence: An Ops operator opens the mandate editor, submits a list that happens to contain a repeated entry, and is told the request failed. It did not fail silently - it destroyed the mandate. Every host onboarded after that point is activated with Aadhaar, PAN and the pet-proofing photo no longer required: reproduced above as a live activation whose only KYC artifact is one manually recorded house check. seedDefaultMandates deliberately refuses to restore (it skips any category with >=1 row, lib/provider-verification-mandate.ts:82), so nothing ever puts the missing checks back, and the staff verification page confidently prints '✓ Eligible to take assignments'.
rule_source: lib/provider-verification-mandate.ts:1-9 module docblock: 'A provider becomes assignment-eligible only when EVERY mandated check for its category is verified. Default mandates ... host → Aadhaar+PAN+house+pet-proofing photo'; and lib/provider-verification-mandate.ts:68-76, which already reasons explicitly about not letting a write silently widen or narrow a category's mandate.
suggested_fix: De-duplicate and validate the full requested set before touching the table (const types=[...new Set(requested)]), and perform the DELETE plus all INSERTs in a single db.batch([...]) so a constraint failure rolls the whole replacement back.

title: The provider's own self-declared services list becomes their matching scope, bypassing the per-category verification mandate entirely
reproduction: /tmp/kyc/p9.mjs (staff-written profile) and /tmp/kyc/p13.mjs (provider-written, through lib/provider-onboarding-self-service.ts). p13 drives createOwnedProviderApplication -> submitOwnedProviderApplication -> ... -> acceptOwnedProviderSla -> saveOwnedProviderProfile with payload.services=['grooming','boarding','pet_taxi'] for an application whose vertical_key is 'grooming'; then staff activateProviderUat + addProviderToServiceMap; then lib/provider-capacity-governance.ts loadGovernedProviders(db,'blr','blr-east',<service>). saveProviderProfile line 44 takes services=arr(p.services) with no allow-list against application.vertical_key; activateProviderUat line 78 writes JSON.stringify(profile.services) straight into provider_capacity_profiles.services_json.
expected: The services a provider can be matched for must be bounded by the vertical their application was approved and verified against, or each additional service must independently satisfy that service's category mandate. A provider whose host mandate says canTakeAssignments:false must not be returned by loadGovernedProviders for 'boarding'.
consequence: The entire per-category verification mandate is opt-out. A groomer who cleared only Aadhaar+PAN types 'boarding' into their own profile form and is then handed overnight boarding assignments by the assignment engine - with house_verification and pet_proofing_photo explicitly still pending on the very same application. loadGovernedProviders is the real eligibility source for app/api/uat-scheduling (assignment offers), lib/universal-replacement-recovery.ts (replacement selection), app/api/training-trainers and lib/haptik-integration-governance.ts serviceability. A customer's dog is left overnight in a home nobody ever inspected.
rule_source: lib/provider-verification-mandate.ts:1-9 ('A provider becomes assignment-eligible only when EVERY mandated check for its category is verified'); lib/provider-onboarding-human-activation.ts:63-67, which states the mandate was wired into activation precisely so 'a host could [not] be activated with house_verification and pet_proofing_photo still not started'.
suggested_fix: Intersect profile.services with the set of services the application's vertical_key authorises before writing services_json in activateProviderUat, and refuse (or route to staff review) any service in saveProviderProfile that is outside the approved vertical. Alternatively make loadGovernedProviders join provider_verifications and require the mandate for the requested serviceCode's category to be allVerified.

title: A boarding host's customer-facing 'KYC verified' badge is a hardcoded seed constant; a real host who clears every mandated check reads as kycVerified:false
reproduction: /tmp/kyc/p15.mjs. Drive a full boarding journey, satisfy all four host-mandate checks (house_verification + pet_proofing_photo via recordManualVerification, aadhaar + pan as verified provider_verifications rows), activateProviderUat, addProviderToServiceMap, then call lib/host-badges.ts computeHostStats(db, providerId) for the real host and for the seeded 'host_sana'. lib/boarding-governance.ts:13-17 is a fixed array with kyc:'verified', background:'verified', homeVerified:1 for four provider ids; line 37 INSERT OR IGNOREs them into boarding_host_profiles. Grepping every INSERT/UPDATE against boarding_host_profiles in lib/ and app/ yields exactly that one seed statement. ensureBoardingGovernanceTables is reached from ensureBoardingStayLifecycleTables (lib/boarding-stay-lifecycle.ts:9), i.e. from ordinary boarding discovery/lifecycle traffic, with no environment gate.
expected: kycVerified / homeVerified shown to a customer must be derived from the provider's actual verification record (provider_verifications / verificationMandateStatus), not from a literal in a seed array. A host who has cleared the full host mandate must read kycVerified:true; a host with zero verification evidence must never read true.
consequence: The trust signal a customer acts on when handing over their pet is inverted. The only hosts a customer can see marked 'KYC verified' and 'home verified' are four rows written by 'founder_seed' with zero verification evidence anywhere in the system, and this seed runs on any database the boarding code touches with no environment flag guarding it. A genuinely fully-verified host shows kycVerified:false. lib/host-badges.ts:115 renders a badge off this value.
rule_source: NONE -> decision ledger. The question nobody has answered: which table is the authority for a boarding host's KYC state - provider_verifications (owned by the verification mandate) or boarding_host_profiles.kyc_status (read by discovery and badges)? Today they are two disconnected registries and only the second has any writer, a hardcoded one.
suggested_fix: Make boarding_host_profiles.kyc_status/home_verified derived from verificationMandateStatus for the host category (or drop the columns and read the mandate directly in host-badges/discovery), and gate the founder_seed host array behind an explicit UAT-seed environment flag so it cannot appear in a real database.

title: IDfy callback deduplication keys on event id alone, so a redelivery carrying a DIFFERENT outcome is answered 200 accepted with the OLD outcome and silently discarded
reproduction:
/tmp/kyc/p8.mjs steps 1 and 2, with a real HMAC over `${stamp}.${rawBody}` via idfyHmacHex and a stubbed submission transport (our contract only - no real IDfy account exists here):
  send({event_id:'EV1',request_id:'IDFY-REQ-001',status:'completed',result:{verification_status:'verified'}})
  send({event_id:'EV1',request_id:'IDFY-REQ-001',status:'completed',result:{verification_status:'not_verified'}})
Line 112 selects on provider_event_id alone; payload_sha256 is computed at line 104 and stored at line 121 but never compared.
measured_before:
-- 1. verified callback --
{"accepted":true,"status":200,"applicationId":"POAPP-TEST-1","verificationType":"aadhaar","outcome":"verified","duplicate":false}
row: [ { verification_type: 'aadhaar', status: 'verified', updated_by: 'idfy_callback' } ]
-- 2. SAME event_id, DIFFERENT payload saying failed --
{"accepted":true,"status":200,"applicationId":"POAPP-TEST-1","verificationType":"aadhaar","outcome":"verified","duplicate":true}
row: [ { verification_type: 'aadhaar', status: 'verified' } ]
callback rows: [ { provider_event_id: 'EV1', outcome: 'verified', accepted: 1, payload_sha256: 'e682238998014d342625fab781f0c461d7abe05b000e7cc5fa476f02f803e352' } ]
expected: The replay key must bind the payload, not just the event id. A delivery whose payload_sha256 differs from the stored one is not a redelivery - it should either be applied (subject to the existing monotonic rule) or refused loudly, but it must never be answered accepted:true with a stale outcome that the caller then reports as the truth.
consequence: A revocation delivered under a reused or colliding event id is dropped, IDfy is told 200 (stop retrying), and the returned body asserts the old 'verified' outcome to whatever called the route. A provider whose Aadhaar was revoked stays verified and assignment-eligible with no trace anywhere except a payload hash nobody compares. The rest of this boundary is well built (503 on absent secret, absolute-difference freshness window, constant-time compare, terminal-state monotonicity - all verified in the same run); this is the one hole left.
rule_source: lib/idfy-callback-boundary.ts:17-19 and 106-113, which state the dedup contract as 'a redelivery ... answers 200 and changes no state' - a delivery with different content is not a redelivery, and the code already stores the hash that would tell the two apart.
suggested_fix: Include payload_sha256 in the replay lookup at line 112 (or compare it after the match) and treat a same-event-id/different-hash delivery as a fresh callback routed through the normal correlation and monotonic-update path.
